title: The One-Power Erdős Conjecture for Primes $p \equiv 7 \pmod{36}$
summary: A conjecture of Erdős asserts that every odd integer $n > 1$ can be written as $n = 2^a + m$, where $a \ge 0$ is an integer and $m$ is a squarefree positive integer. We study this conjecture for primes $p \equiv 7 \pmod{36}$. Writing $x = (p-1)/6$, the candidate remainders take the shapes $p - 1 = 6x$, $p-2 = 6x-1$, $p-4 = 3(2x-1)$, and $p-8 = 6x-7$, in which the primes $2$ and $3$ are completely controlled: every obstruction to squarefreeness comes from a prime $q \ge 5$.
